a: A network covering a small area, such as one site, where the organisation owns the hardware
A network covering a large area using rented telecoms links
A computer that isn't connected to anything
The undersea cables between continents
tasks.fb: LAN = local area network: one site, and the organisation owns the hardware.

tasks.q: Which is the best example of a WAN?
a: The internet
A school network
A home Wi-Fi network
A printer connected by USB
tasks.fb: The internet is the biggest WAN, joining networks all over the world.

tasks.q: Which of these is a disadvantage of networking?
a: Viruses can spread from one computer to others
Files can be shared
Printers can be shared
Backups can be done centrally
tasks.fb: The other three are all advantages of networks.

a: The amount of data that can be sent in a given time, such as per second
The length of a network cable
The number of devices on a network
The range of a Wi-Fi signal
tasks.fb: Bandwidth is measured in bits per second. More bandwidth means more data can be sent at once.

tasks.q: Thirty students start streaming video at the same time. Why does the network slow down?
a: More users are sharing the same bandwidth
The cables heat up
The switch changes its MAC address
The videos are stored on each computer
tasks.fb: Each user gets a smaller share of the available bandwidth, so everything slows down.

tasks.q: The school wants more CCTV cameras recording video to the file server. What should the network manager check first?
a: Whether the network has enough bandwidth for the extra video traffic
Whether the cameras record in colour
How many printers the school has
Whether the cameras are made by the same company
tasks.fb: Video creates a lot of traffic. Extra cameras could use up bandwidth and slow the network for everyone, and the server needs enough storage too.

tasks.q: In a client-server network, what does the server do?
a: Provides services such as file storage, logins and backups to the clients
Requests files from the clients
Acts as an equal peer like every other computer
Connects the LAN to the internet
tasks.fb: Clients request services and the server provides them. Connecting to the internet is the router's job.

tasks.q: Which of these is an advantage of a peer-to-peer network?
a: It is cheaper to set up, because no expensive server is needed
It is easier to back up all the shared data
It is more secure
It is easier to manage file security
tasks.fb: The other three are advantages of client-server networks.

tasks.q: Torrenting downloads parts of a file from many other users' computers at once. Which model is this?
a: Peer-to-peer
Client-server
A star network
A standalone computer
tasks.fb: Every user's computer shares pieces of the file directly with the others, so they act as peers.

tasks.q: What is the difference between a switch and a router?
a: A switch connects devices within a LAN; a router connects different networks, such as a LAN and the internet
A router connects devices within a LAN; a switch connects the LAN to the internet
There is no difference
A switch is wireless and a router is wired
tasks.fb: Switches work inside a LAN using MAC addresses. Routers join networks together using IP addresses.

tasks.q: Which device lets wireless devices connect to a wired network?
a: A wireless access point (WAP)
A switch
A UTP cable
A fibre optic cable
tasks.fb: A WAP sends and receives radio waves and is connected to the wired network by cable.

tasks.q: Why is fibre optic used instead of UTP to link buildings that are far apart?
a: It carries data much further with high bandwidth, and isn't affected by electrical interference
It is cheaper and easier to install
It uses radio waves
It plugs straight into any laptop
tasks.fb: UTP is limited to about 100 m per run. Fibre works over kilometres, although it costs more.

a: A worldwide collection of connected computer networks
All the websites in the world
One huge computer owned by a tech company
The Wi-Fi in your home
tasks.fb: The internet is the network of networks. The websites on it are the World Wide Web, which is a service that uses the internet.

a: Turns a domain name, such as www.google.com, into an IP address
Stores the web pages for every website
Gives each device its MAC address
Encrypts Wi-Fi signals
tasks.fb: DNS is made up of many domain name servers that look up the IP address for a domain name.

tasks.q: Which of these is a disadvantage of using the cloud?
a: It relies on a stable internet connection
You can access your data anywhere, at any time
It is easy to scale up
It has good backup and recovery options
tasks.fb: The other three are advantages of the cloud. Other disadvantages include ongoing costs and less control over your data.

tasks.q: In a star network, what happens if the central switch fails?
a: Every device loses its connection
Only one device is affected
Data is rerouted around the switch
Nothing happens
tasks.fb: The switch is a single point of failure.

tasks.q: Why is a mesh network more reliable than a star network?
a: Data can be rerouted along another path if a link fails
It uses less cable
It has a central switch
Every device is wireless
tasks.fb: Mesh networks have many routes between devices, so there is no single point of failure.

tasks.q: The internet is an example of which topology?
a: Partial mesh
Star
Full mesh
Standalone
tasks.fb: Routers connect to several other routers, but not to every one of them.

tasks.q: Put the steps in order, from typing the address to seeing the page.
steps: You type www.google.com into the browser
The browser asks a DNS server for the IP address of www.google.com
DNS servers look up the domain name, asking other DNS servers if they need to
The IP address is sent back to the browser
The browser uses the IP address to request the page from the web server, which sends it back
tasks.fb: DNS is not one server but many domain name servers working together. You don't need their names for the exam, just the idea.

info.title: Exam tip: LAN vs WAN
info.text: Compare both area and ownership: a LAN covers one site and the organisation owns the hardware; a WAN covers a large area and uses links rented from telecoms companies.

info.title: Exam tip: performance
info.text: Name the factor and explain its effect, for example: more users share the same bandwidth, so each user gets less and data transfers more slowly.

info.title: Exam tip: client-server
info.text: Say what the server does (provides files, logins, backups) and what the clients do (request services). Just writing 'has a server' won't get the marks.

info.title: Exam tip: switch vs router
info.text: A switch connects devices within a LAN using MAC addresses. A router connects networks together using IP addresses. Make the comparison in one sentence.

info.title: Exam tip: DNS
info.text: DNS is not one server: it is many domain name servers. You don't need to name them, just explain that they turn a domain name into an IP address.

info.title: Exam tip: topologies
info.text: For star, mention the single point of failure. For mesh, mention rerouting, and the cost of the extra cabling.
